anomalies.observed: On the I2C-sensors sheet the PDIS pin (8) of both ADM3260 isolators (U10 for pH, U6 for EC) is labelled NET0003, and on the peristaltic-pump sheet the PD/UART pin (8) of all three TMC2209 drivers (U3, U5, U8) is also labelled NET0003; the SoC connects NET0003 to its single-wire UART pin group through R34 (1k). Thus the EZO isolator power-disable line and the stepper single-wire UART bus (STEP_BUS) are merged onto one net.
anomalies.expected: The specification treats these as two separate signals: the EZO_PDIS net ties U3/U4 pin 8 to ESP32 IO6/SPI_CLK, while the shared TMC2209 UART (STEP_BUS) is on IO21/IO22. They must remain distinct nets so firmware can power-cycle the pH/EC isolators independently of the stepper bus.

evidence.quote: An EZO_PDIS net ties both U3 pin 8 and U4 pin 8 (PDIS) to a single ESP32 pin (IO6/SPI_CLK) [§4.2]
U10 pin 8 PDIS and U6 pin 8 PDIS carry label NET0003; U3/U5/U8 pin 8 PD/UART carry label NET0003 (sheets 1 and 2)

anomalies.impact: The pH/EC isolator power-disable pin is shorted to the stepper UART bus. Any activity on the UART line (or its idle pull-up via R34) will enable/disable the galvanically isolated I2C bridges to the EZO-pH and EZO-EC circuits, and the PDIS pins load the UART bus. Firmware can no longer power-cycle the probes independently of the dosing drivers, corrupting I2C sensor reads and stepper communication.
